title: IVR scripts
blurb: The module vocabulary, branches, Skill Transfer, queries, and visual framing.
summary: Scripts are named modules. The builder speaks that vocabulary and does not pretend to export a VCC file.

lessons.title: The module list is the vocabulary
objectives: Treat the bench file as a model
paragraphs: The IVR modules chapter names the blocks you may place. The list includes Play, Menu, Get Digits, Input, Voice Input, If/Else, Case, Set Variable, Lookup Contact Record, Query, Skill Transfer, IVA Transfer, Voicemail Transfer, Set DNC, Third Party Transfer, Foreign Script, Language, and others such as Conference, Iterator, and the Salesforce modules.

This lab's builder uses those names. It does not contain a module called Hangup, because that name is not in the chapter list this lab read. A transfer that completes the script is the ending the skill article describes.
uncertain: Some third-party notes mention a hangup behavior. It is not in the modules chapter quoted here.

lessons.title: Play, Menu, digits, and voice
objectives: Store digits in a named variable
paragraphs: Play speaks a prompt or TTS. Menu takes a choice and has an exit per option. Get Digits and Input collect what the caller types. Voice Input and the Natural Language Processing module are the speech-side blocks in the same chapter. Input is what the ZIP-code web-service example uses, storing ZIP as a variable.
A menu that has no No Match path strands people who press the wrong key. Draw that exit before you draw option 1.

lessons.title: If/Else is two ways. Case is more
objectives: Match branch count to the module
paragraphs: If/Else has two branches. The modules chapter includes both If/Else and Case. When you need three or more outcomes, Case is the block that exists for that. Nesting If/Else until the drawing looks like a hedge is how scripts become unreviewable.
The condition is your expression: open hours, a variable, a lookup result. The module does not know your business. It evaluates what you typed.

lessons.title: Skill Transfer has more than a skill name
objectives: Count the tabs in the editor
Prefer one skill when you need the report
paragraphs: The community article lists General, Skills, Announcement, Priority, Connectors, Queue Callback, and Disposition. It also says 'six tabs' and then names more than six. Count the tabs in your editor. Do not trust the word six.

Multiple skills mean any agent who has one of them may get the call. The article says Five9 recommends one skill in the module if you want useful reports. No skill selected sends calls toward users with no skills, labeled Default. Pause Before Transfer defaults to 0 and is not On Hold in a report. The default disposition named in that article is Abandon.
uncertain: The article says six tabs and then lists seven names. The editor is the count that matters.

lessons.title: Variables, lookup, and query
objectives: Keep script variables and reporting variables apart
paragraphs: Set Variable writes a value. Lookup Contact Record reads the contact. Query calls out, and the published example is an XML web service POST whose response groups are mapped with regular expressions into variables. That example uses script variables, not call variables, because the caller is not connected to an agent.

Call variables are a different object, used when you need reporting later. Enabling them does not backfill history. A Query result you never store in a reporting call variable will not appear in a historical call log.

figure.caption: The example is careful about this.

lessons.title: IVA, foreign scripts, DNC, and leaving the platform
objectives: Keep digital IVA and voice IVA in their own notes
paragraphs: IVA Transfer hands the call to a Studio task. Foreign Script jumps to another IVR script. Set DNC is the removal action. Third Party Transfer leaves your agents. Language switches prompt language. These are five different exits. A diagram that says 'send to bot' does not say which one.

Digital IVA integration, in the March 2026 Studio article, needs a Studio API key with Build permission and a ChatBot task key pasted into the VCC side. Voice IVA Transfer is not automatically that digital article. Confirm which channel you are wiring.
uncertain: Public pages describe IVA Transfer and a digital ChatBot integration separately. This lab does not claim they share one property sheet.

lessons.title: Visual IVR and frames
objectives: Protect visual IVR from hostile frames
paragraphs: The technical requirements say administrators can apply web page security so a Visual IVR script is not embedded in a frame where the user can be hijacked. The mechanism named is the X-Frame-Options header. The browser table in that PDF lists old versions and tells you to test others.
A visual script is still a script: prompts, branches, and a handoff. Framing is an extra threat. Do not treat a 2016-era browser row as the current support list. The PDF says to retest.
